newsitem.title: CANADA: Ivaco finalizes contracts for rod mill.
newsitem.headline: Ivaco finalizes contracts for rod mill.

text.p: Ivaco Inc said on Tuesday it has finalized contracts with suppliers for its L'Orignal rod mill expansion to bring Ivaco's Rolling Mills annual production of wire rods to 950,000 tons from 700,000 tons.

Ivaco said the project will be completed in 1998 with all rolling equipment and overall mill design purchased from Morgan Construction Co, supporting electronics, product tracking softwares and automation purchased from General Electric, the coil handling system will be supplied by Sund Birsta of Sweden and the reheat furnace will be supplied by Danieli Centro Combustion of Milan.

The Montreal-based steelmaker said as part of the first phase of the development Ivaco Rolling Mills will install a new Morgan mini blocks, a new Stelmor rod cooling line and upgrade the the existing automation controlling mill operations.
In the second phase Ivaco will install a new walking beam reheating furnace, a Morgan housingless stand breakdown mill and a Tekisun reducing-sizing mill.

"No other existing rod mill combines all the features of Ivaco's newly modernized mill," said Ivaco president chief executive officer, Paul Ivanier. "We believe these changes will make this mill the most modern, highest quality and lowest cost rod mill in North America. We will be producing rod coils of up to 6,000 lbs and our finishing speed will increase from 16,700 feet to 23,600 feet per minute.
